column3: Steadfast feet against disbelievers offer a distant contrast to placing misleaders beneath one's feet.
It carries present blindness into a more severe afterlife misguidance, supplying the focus's judgment horizon.
It joins jinn and humans under the same fulfilled judgment, directly framing the two classes named in the focus.
The prayer for firm feet in conflict is an opposite and limited use of the focus's feet imagery.
The disbelievers' effort to suppress the Quran provides a nearby mechanism by which others can be turned from guidance.
Those seeking to mislead others ultimately mislead themselves, directly limiting the blame the focus directs at misleaders.
It exposes the reciprocal jinn-human relationship at final gathering and assigns both groups to the Fire.
Nearby disbelief in the Hereafter supplies only general background for the condemned speakers.
Loss falls upon the people themselves when their fabricated supports vanish, reinforcing retained personal responsibility.
Its failure of family proximity to transfer righteousness only broadly parallels the focus's question of shared responsibility.
The inmates' plea for relief shares the Fire setting but neither identifies misleaders nor reverses their rank.
Human and jinn devils jointly deceive through alluring speech, directly identifying the visible and hidden misleaders sought in the focus.
In judgment the weak directly blame the arrogant for their disbelief, closely paralleling the focus's accusation of prior leaders.
Nearby companions beautify error before the same jinn-and-human judgment, providing an immediate cause for the focus's blame.
Its descent to the lowest rank resonates with the status reversal desired for the misleaders.
The condemned explicitly say that obeying their leaders caused their misguidance, a direct parallel to the focus's complaint.
The earlier rejection of the messengers is nearby opposition context but does not clarify misleaders or their punishment.
Idols are said to have led many people astray, offering a direct but non-judgment-scene example of misleading agents.
Later communities in the Fire accuse earlier ones of leading them astray and request doubled punishment, closely matching the focus.
Guidance and the restoration of the martyrs' condition do not illuminate blame, misdirection, or rank reversal.
Punishment is tied to what people themselves sent ahead, correcting any attempt to displace all responsibility onto misleaders.
Its joint naming of jinn and humans establishes their shared moral orientation, though not their misleading relation.
The nearby warning of forgiveness and painful punishment gives only a general judgment background.
Water and a voice beneath Mary use lower spatial position without the focus's hierarchy or blame.
The weak blame the arrogant leaders' continual plotting for their disbelief, directly developing culpability between followers and leaders.
The Samiri is explicitly named as the one who led the people astray, though outside the focus's final judgment scene.
People in Hell blame those who sent the punishment ahead of them, a close parallel to retrospective accusation of predecessors.
Jinn and humans are jointly described as more astray and destined for Hell, supplying the focus's shared eschatological setting.
Nearby rejection of the Reminder is general opposition context rather than an account of who misled whom.
Showing Moses the great signs does not relate to revealing misleaders or reversing their standing.
The plotters are made the lowest, providing a status-reversal parallel without the focus's causal blame relation.
The challenge to show a rival creation and the verdict of manifest error combine disclosure with misguidance, but not misleading agents.
Judgment by what God has shown offers a broad disclosure theme without the focus's final blame or hierarchy.
Jinn and humans receive warning, then testify against themselves as disbelievers at the final meeting, closely framing their shared accountability.
Nearby disbelief in revelation is called remote misguidance, giving a close surah context for the condemned group's error.
It contrasts believers' firmness with wrongdoers' misguidance, supplying an outcome frame but not a human intermediary.
The prayer not to become a trial for disbelievers is only a broad concern about causing others to go astray.
Criminals are located in misguidance and blazing punishment, providing the judgment outcome behind the focus's accusation.
The believers' peaceful entry into gardens is not connected to the focus's condemned misleaders.
The disbelievers' claim that believers are not guided shows polemical mislabeling, not causal misdirection or judgmental blame.
The immediately adjacent testimony of the skins develops the final disclosure setting in which the focus's speakers make their request.
The brothers' mistaken charge that their father is astray is a domestic accusation without the focus's moral or eschatological structure.
Pharaoh's elite use wealth and splendor to lead people from God's path, then face a request for punishment after seeing it.
The people's wandering offers a spatial image of loss but no misleader, final accusation, or rank reversal.
The guilty label believers as astray, a false social accusation that only distantly contrasts with the focus's actual misleaders.
God makes the disbelievers' word the lowest, paralleling the focus's wish to lower those responsible for misguidance.
The revival of the earth does not address misguidance, judgmental disclosure, or social hierarchy.
Human transgression is a broad moral antecedent to judgment but has no link to misleading agents.
What lies beneath the soil is a cosmological spatial reference unrelated to the focus's feet imagery.
The keepers recall rejected messengers and describe the disbelievers' plea as astray, linking final suffering to prior refusal.
Those struck for what their hands sent ahead appeal for a messenger, reinforcing responsibility before final complaint.
The speakers admit their own wrongdoing, a limited corrective to blaming another for their condition.
The disappearance of invoked partners and recognition of no escape provide a nearby final-judgment disclosure parallel.
The supposed objects of worship reveal that people were in fact devoted to jinn, directly uncovering a hidden misleading allegiance.
The demand to see God openly shares only the language of seeing, not disclosure of culpable agents.
The rejecters call following a messenger misguidance, a reversed accusation without the focus's judgment or leaders.
Calling the messenger a mad poet does not establish a relevant jinn-human misleading or rank relation.
Provision from above and beneath feet is positive abundance, not the subordination of misleaders.
The ordering and adornment of the heavens are unrelated to final blame or moral rank.
Disputing the Hour is called remote misguidance, supplying only a general eschatological backdrop.
Punishment from beneath feet is a physical threat, not the focus's act of lowering culpable misleaders.
Firming believers' feet is an opposite use of the image and does not concern blame for misguidance.
Moses identifies Satan as an open enemy and misleader, offering a direct hidden-agent parallel outside the final scene.
Punishment from above and beneath feet shares bodily spatial imagery but not the focus's status reversal.
The nearby principle that evil returns against oneself directly preserves personal accountability alongside blame of misleaders.
Its joint mention of human and jinn sinners gives a concise final-judgment frame for the two classes in the focus.
The city's inversion is a punishment reversal but has no relation to misleaders being made low.
Aaron identifies the calf as a trial and calls the people back to obedience, providing an antecedent to being misled.
Being found lost and then guided uses a different personal and favorable sense of misguidance.
The overturned city supplies a punishment inversion without the focus's causal or social hierarchy.
The nearby dispute over Moses' Book gives only broad revelation-rejection context.
The brothers' repeated charge against their father is a false family judgment without relevant final accountability.
The speaker's regret at having sent deeds ahead gives a direct final reckoning contrast to deflecting blame onto others.
The angels' unwearied worship does not clarify the focus's disbelievers or their misleaders.
Following unknowing desires describes a self-sustaining path of misguidance that complicates blame of external leaders.
Those condemned admit that they led others astray as they themselves went astray, directly addressing layered responsibility for misguidance.
The command to worship the Creator rather than celestial objects gives nearby monotheistic context but no blame relation.
Disbelievers who obstruct God's way have their deeds lost, identifying agents who actively turn others from guidance.
Resurrection denial supplies only a general background for the focus's future judgment setting.
Nearby association and disbelief in the Creator establish opposition context but not a misleading relation.
The mention of humans and jinn concerns prior physical contact, not their shared accountability or misguidance.
Misleaders invite believers to follow their path and falsely offer to bear their sins, directly refuting transferred responsibility.
Those in the Fire ask who brought this upon them and seek doubled punishment, closely paralleling the focus's retrospective blame.
Believers' prayer for protection from the Fire has no relation to misleaders or lowered rank.
The denial that the messenger is astray offers a limited contrast to accusations of being led astray.
Disbelieving leaders coerce messengers toward their religion, showing an active attempt to redirect others from guidance.
Divine knowledge of who strays gives only a broad classification of guidance and misguidance.
The elite reject a messenger and protect inherited norms, illustrating social leadership that can divert a community from guidance.
Human striving will be shown, reinforcing the focus's final demand that responsible agents be made visible.
Adam and Eve confess their own wrongdoing and loss, providing a direct counterpoint to exclusive blame of others.
The mention of a multitude from earlier peoples does not develop misguidance, judgment, or rank.
Human creation from a clinging substance is unrelated to the focus's human-and-jinn accountability.
Those who claim others would have been safe by obeying them are challenged to avert death, exposing the limits of such leadership claims.
The jinn's creation from fire identifies one class in the focus but adds no misleading or judgmental relation.
People called to God's Book for judgment turn away, showing voluntary refusal that remains their own responsibility.
After truth arrives, guidance and misguidance return upon each person, directly qualifying the focus's blame of external misleaders.
Patience and trust in God do not bear on the condemned speakers' accusation or status reversal.
Mary's instruction to speak of seeing a human has no connection to final disclosure or misdirection.
The death of disbelieving transgressors gives a broad consequence context without identifying misleaders.
The wavering person has no path when left astray, supplying an outcome image of misguidance without an intermediary.
Those who were followed disown their followers when they see the punishment, directly staging the rupture behind the focus's accusation.
The followers wish to return so they can disown their former leaders, closely paralleling the focus's desire to reverse the relationship.
A party from the People of the Book seeks to turn believers back into disbelief, directly identifying human agents of misguidance.
Satan's aim is to lead those appealing to false judgment far astray, giving a direct hidden-agent parallel.
False worship is linked to the rebellious Satan, locating a hidden misleading agent behind visible religious practice.
Satan explicitly vows to lead people astray, directly supplying the agency named in the focus.
Earlier people both went astray and led many astray, a concise direct formulation of layered misguidance.
Devils bewilder a person while companions call him back to guidance, directly contrasting hidden misleading pressure with true guidance.
Satan declares that he will lie in wait on the straight path, providing a direct mechanism of attempted misguidance.
Satan's approach from every direction develops the obstructing agency stated in the preceding verse.
Satan whispers to Adam and his wife in order to expose and deceive them, a direct hidden-agent example.
Satan causes them to fall through deception, directly joining misdirection to culpable agency.
Those who take devils as protectors think themselves guided while they are astray, directly exposing hidden misleaders.
The earlier group denies superiority to the later and confirms that each must taste punishment, directly limiting blame transfer in the Fire.
Satan beautifies the disbelievers' deeds, then disowns them when punishment appears, closely matching final exposure of a misleader.
Those who manipulate sacred time lead disbelievers astray, supplying a human practice that redirects others from guidance.
On the Day of gathering, alleged partners deny that their worshippers served them, adding a direct judgment-scene disavowal.
Pharaoh leads his people on the Day of Resurrection into the Fire, an exceptionally close leader-and-follower judgment parallel.
The weak tell the arrogant that they followed them and ask whether they can remove any part of the Fire, directly paralleling the focus.
Satan denies having authority and tells his followers to blame themselves, directly qualifying the focus's effort to place all blame on misleaders.
Those who set up rivals lead others from God's way, directly identifying a humanly enacted form of misguidance.
Satan vows to make wrongdoing attractive and lead people astray, supplying an explicit hidden-agent cause.
Misleaders bear burdens of those they lead astray as well as their own, directly articulating layered responsibility.
Those who associated partners identify them on the Day of Judgment, while the partners reject their claim, extending the disclosure of false allegiances.
Those who disbelieve and turn people from God's way receive punishment added for their corruption, directly marking responsibility for misleading others.
Satan is authorized to provoke and entice people by every available means, supplying a broad mechanism of misleading pressure.
Abraham warns that serving Satan makes one a follower of the hidden misleader, directly joining allegiance and misguidance.
Satan whispers to Adam with a deceptive offer, giving a direct instance of a hidden agent leading a human astray.
Adam's disobedience is explicitly described as going astray, preserving the individual's responsibility after deceptive prompting.
Following divine guidance prevents going astray, providing the positive alternative to the focus's blamed misdirection.
Whoever takes Satan as an ally is led astray by him and guided toward the punishment of the Blaze.
Turning arrogantly from God's way is described as leading astray, linking social opposition to humiliation in the Hereafter.
God asks the worshipped beings whether they led the servants astray or the servants strayed themselves, directly posing the focus's responsibility question.
The worshipped beings deny divinity and explain the worshippers' forgetfulness, extending the distinction between external objects and personal culpability.
Hell is exposed to those who went astray, supplying the final setting in which false allegiances are uncovered.
The false gods and the misguided are thrown together into Hell, directly joining misleading objects and their followers in judgment.
The condemned confess that they were in clear error when they equated others with the Lord, retaining their own culpability.
The condemned say that criminals led them astray, an exact direct parallel to the focus's complaint against misleaders.
At judgment the idolaters are asked where their alleged partners are, opening the same disclosure of false guidance.
The alleged partners are summoned but do not answer, and the worshippers see the punishment, directly exposing failed guides at judgment.
Those who mislead others bear additional burdens along with their own, directly establishing non-transferable but layered responsibility.
Former friends disown one another and curse one another on the Day of Resurrection, a related reversal of prior allegiance.
Some purchase distracting discourse to lead people from God's way without knowledge, directly identifying an active human mechanism of misguidance.
Appeal to inherited practice resists guidance, supplying a social route through which followers remain on error.
The condemned ask for their leaders to receive a doubled punishment and a great curse, directly continuing the focus's punitive wish against misleaders.
The arrogant deny physically barring the weak but identify their prior guilt, directly continuing the judgment dispute over who caused disbelief.
Satan is declared an enemy who invites his followers to the Blaze, directly joining hidden misguidance to final punishment.
The command not to worship Satan identifies him as an open enemy, clarifying the hidden allegiance implicated in the focus.
Satan is said to have led many multitudes astray, an explicit broad statement of his misleading agency.
Followers accuse prior leaders of approaching them from a position of authority, closely matching retrospective blame in the Fire.
The leaders deny coercive authority and identify the followers as transgressors, directly complicating unilateral blame.
The leaders admit leading their followers astray because they were themselves astray, an exact account of layered misguidance.
Both leaders and followers share the punishment on that Day, directly resolving the focus's hierarchy dispute within common liability.
The weak in the Fire tell the arrogant that they followed them and ask for relief from the Fire, a very close parallel.
The arrogant answer that all are in the Fire and that God has judged between servants, directly rejecting the followers' attempt to shift the punishment.
Whoever turns from the Reminder receives a satanic companion, directly linking rejection to a hidden misleader.
At judgment the follower wishes there were the farthest distance between himself and his satanic companion, closely echoing the focus's hostile reversal.
Wrongdoers learn that shared punishment offers no relief, directly preserving common liability despite prior misleading relations.
Satan urges disbelief and then disowns the person when he disbelieves, a direct pattern of deception followed by abandonment.
The whisperer withdraws after insinuation, supplying the hidden form of misleading agency.
The whisperer works within human breasts, identifying the inward mechanism through which misguidance is induced.
The whispering agents are explicitly from jinn and humankind, directly matching the two classes named in the focus.
